meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so you have twenty minutes. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before he saw it on his phone in the middle of class?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. That's one. Now tell me what you based the zero on, because if the answer is a piece of software, we're going to have a short meeting.

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.

Turn the screen, Hale, I want to read it myself, and I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. Owen tells me he wrote it over the weekend. Before you entered anything, did anyone ask him where those words were before 11:52?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.

I'm writing down Act 3, Scene 2, and I'll check it tonight, line by line. You still haven't told me whether anyone asked Owen about any of this before the zero. Whatever happens next, Hale, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

Thursday at 8:15, your room, before his classmates arrive, and nobody else in the building hears about it. I'll agree to that to put this behind him, Hale, but I want an email from you tonight saying nothing goes on his record, cc the principal. Who else has seen this file so far?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today that Owen will complete a supervised rewrite in your room on Thursday at 8:15 with the vice-principal supervising, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will go on his record. I still require that commitment in writing, along with the name of everyone who has seen this file. I expect that confirmation from you tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15, and she still wants written confirmation that nothing goes on Owen's record and a list of everyone who has seen the file.
What moved her: showing the version history with its exact times, because it was specific, tied to Owen's own document, and something she could read herself.
What cost ground: leaving her question about whether Owen was heard before the zero unanswered twice, because procedure is exactly what she watches and the silence kept her guarded.
Try next time: when she first asked whether anyone spoke to Owen before he saw the zero, answer that plainly right after your apology, before you put the version history on the screen.
